title: Cognitive Load Minimizer — sketchpad
summary: Notes and rough PRD-style thinking for a lightweight feature to reduce cognitive overhead in longer multi-turn LLM sessions. Goal: help end-users maintain focus and make decisions faster by surfacing distilled context, actionable hints, and temporary UI modes that hide noise.
body:
Problem statement:
- Users in multi-turn sessions often feel overwhelmed: too much prior context, competing suggestions, and UI controls. This leads to longer latency in decision-making, more follow-up clarifying prompts, and higher token consumption as people re-state context.

Hypothesis:
- If we provide a transient 'focus' experience that (a) surfaces a one-line distilled context, (b) reduces peripheral affordances, and (c) suggests 1–3 next-step actions, then users will complete tasks faster, send fewer clarifying messages, and consume fewer tokens.

Primary goals (product):
- Reduce user cognitive load in 3-minute+ sessions.
- Improve task completion rate for goal-directed flows (e.g., drafting, code edits, troubleshooting).
- Lower median tokens-per-task by eliminating redundant clarifications.

User stories / scenarios:
- As a marketing writer, I want a concise recap of the thread so I can continue editing without re-reading the whole conversation.
- As a developer debugging infra, I want the assistant to surface the minimal relevant state plus 2 suggested next actions (re-run, check logs) so I can act quickly.
- As a product manager running research, I want a temporary compact UI to craft a follow-up prompt without being distracted by older branches.

Proposed feature surface (UX sketches in words):
1) Focus Toggle (ephemeral): small pill UI; when enabled: shrink header, collapse older messages into "condensed stack" (hover to expand), and pin a single "session summary" line.
2) Distillation Line: AI-generated one-line summary of current active objective + 1 bullet of important constraints (confidence score). Editable by the user.
3) Action Suggestions: 1–3 short CTA buttons derived from intent classification (e.g., "Refine prompt", "Run unit test", "Shorten reply"). Each CTA maps to a templated prompt or route (with optional confirm).
4) Noise Dampening: hide or mute non-essential controls (explore threads, model selector) while in focus mode; quick access via a small '...' to restore.
5) Temporary Context Pruning: behind the scenes, mark older messages as lower priority for caching/batching to save token cost; don’t delete — just deprioritize.

Implementation sketches (backend):
- Distillation: small summarization model run on session state when focus toggled or when session idle > 30s. Cache result; allow user edits.
- Intent classifier: tiny on-device/cheap model that maps recent user message + summary to top 3 actions.
- UI flags: front-end state controls which components to hide and wires CTAs to prompt templates.
- Telemetry: record toggles, CTA clicks, summary edits, and tokens consumed before/after.

Success metrics (experiment):
- Primary: median time-to-next-action (seconds) reduced by 15% among focused users.
- Secondary: tokens-per-task down 10%; clarifying-turns per session down 20%; CTA conversion rate > 25%.
- Safety: number of user edits to distillation should be low (<10% large edits) — indicates quality.

Rollout / experiment plan (MVP):
- Phase A (internal): A/B test with 50 internal users (devs, docs team) for 2 weeks. Collect qualitative feedback.
- Phase B (beta): 1% of new hosted API users via feature flag in console + opt-in. 4 week run.
- Observations: track the above metrics + NPS-style quick prompt after session: "Did focus mode help you finish faster?"

Instrumentation / logging details:
- Events: focus_on/off, distill_generated, distill_edited, action_suggested, action_taken, tokens_before_focus, tokens_after_focus, session_length_ms.
- Funnels: focus_open -> CTA_click -> follow-up_message_sent -> task_marked_done.

Risks / open questions:
- Distillation hallucination risk: one-line summary could remove critical constraints. Mitigation: show confidence and allow inline edit; fallback to full view if user expands.
- UX discoverability vs annoyance: toggling must be unobtrusive and easily reversible. Might need onboarding microcopy.
- Cost tradeoffs: running summarization increases infra cost; need cheap model or batched triggers.

Quick experiments to validate low-cost assumptions:
- Simulate distillation using heuristic (first sentence of last N messages) to test UI without inference cost.
- Run offline human evaluation on sample sessions to score distillation fidelity.

Edge cases to consider:
- Multithreaded sessions where the active objective is ambiguous. Possibly tag threads and allow per-thread focus.
- Long-running sessions with ephemeral external state (links, snippets) that cannot be fully summarized. Provide 'open full context' CTA.

Next steps / TODOs:
- Prototype front-end toggle (2 days) + local heuristic distillation to demo to PMs.
- Draft lightweight API payload for distill endpoint (input: session ids + last N messages; output: summary, confidence, hints).
- Spin up internal experiment board (JIRA: DX-781) and lightweight UX mockups.

Notes to self / friction points:
- Need to align with product privacy policy: distillation runs should obey customer privacy modes. Add a flag to disable for Private deployments.
- Coordinate with Serving Runtime team on caching eviction semantics when we mark messages as low priority.

Related/links:
- Reference: internal thread on context-budgeting (confluence://dx/context-budgeting).
- Ticket: JIRA:DX-781 (experiment tracking).

Quick brain dump of alternatives (short list):
- "Minimalist Composer" — always-on compact composer with distilled context above.
- "Stage Mode" — stepper-style UI that forces single-thread progression (heavier commitment).
- "Smart Hints" — purely CTA-driven overlay (no UI collapse).

Final thought (for next sync):
- Keep MVP tiny: toggled UI + one reliable distill template + 2 CTAs. If that moves metrics, iterate on intelligent pruning and cost optimizations.
notes: This is a working pad — rough, incomplete. Save iterations as separate file versions or append date. Prefer quick prototype to long spec at this stage.
